question: Is the Aurzen TravelPlay a good back seat screen for a Tesla Model Y? Where can I buy one?
query: Aurzen TravelPlay review Tesla Model Y compatibility buy official store 2026

replays.text:
**Yes—if you want a big-screen setup for use while the Model Y is parked.** TravelPlay is a foldable **projector screen and sunshade**, not an electronic display, so you’ll need a compatible portable projector. It offers rear-seat, tailgate, and panoramic-roof viewing modes, with clip-in installation and a carry bag. Projection is intended for use only while the car is stationary. ([Aurzen product page](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

**Check your Model Y’s year before buying:** It’s designed for the 2025–2026 Model Y Refresh. Aurzen says it can work with 2020–2024 models in sky-roof mode, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window.

You can buy it from [Aurzen’s U.S. store](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y), listed at **$119.99**. Aurzen lists free shipping, a 30-day money-back guarantee, and a one-year warranty; the product is marked as available in the U.S. only. ([Aurzen](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y))

**Yes—if you want a projector screen for parked-car movie nights, rather than a built-in electronic display.** The TravelPlay is a foldable, clip-in screen and sunshade, with rear-seat, tailgate, and panoramic-roof viewing modes. It offers roughly 47- and 50-inch screen areas and works with an Aurzen ZIP or another compatible projector; **the projector is not included**. Projection is for use only while the car is stationary. [Aurzen’s product listing](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y)

**Check your Model Y’s year before buying:** it’s designed for the 2025–2026 refresh. Aurzen says it can fit 2020–2024 models in roof-viewing mode, but the rear screen won’t fully cover the window.

You can [buy it directly from Aurzen](https://aurzen.com/collections/new-releases/products/aurzen-travelplay-autocinema-screen-for-tesla-model-y). The listing shows **$119.99** and says it’s available in the U.S.; Aurzen also advertises free shipping, a 30-day money-back guarantee, and a one-year warranty.

**Yes—if you want a projector screen, not a standalone video display.** TravelPlay clips into the Model Y and doubles as a sunshade, with rear-seat, tailgate, and panoramic-roof viewing setups. You’ll need a compatible portable projector, and projection is for when the car is parked.

Fit is best for the **2025–2026 Model Y Refresh**.
